item.title: Comment on Markets in everything? by H
item.description:
$500 billion is 3x Ukraine’s GDP and comparable to the Versailles reparations imposed on Germany in today’s dollars. It seems like it would be pretty dumb for Ukraine to agree to this, even if the alternative is ceding territory to Russia.

And if the US is going to do stuff like this, it seems like other countries could do it for a lot cheaper. Beat Rwanda, a small impoverished African state, for all the minerals in the DRC, which are surely worth hundreds of billions? China would probably do it for 1/10th of the minerals. Seems like a bad equilibrium for the most militaristic countries to extract protection money like this.

item.title: Comment on Hire Don’t Fire at the FDA by Steven
item.description:
Reply to MP:

And it would be wrong about every agency.

Firing provisional employees in a government that is already wildly overspending is anything but ignorant, and Alex' call for additional employees at FDA is anything but smart.

If Alex had anything smart to say about FDA firings, he'd be showing us how to rearrange the agency to accomplish its most important goals withing the confines of a balanced budget.

The government is not "wildly overspending", at least not on the core bureaucratic functions. The size of the federal workforce has grown slowly in real numbers, but has actually declined as a fraction of the population (https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/01/07/what-the-data-says-about-federal-workers/).

The federal budget problems are caused by spending on old people, the military, and debt. Those problems will not be fixed by firing people, because the obligations those people were addressing still exist. It is also clearly not an actual goal of the administration since they are also pushing a tax cut and suggesting mailing everyone a check for the supposed money they are saving.

If you want to reduce the debt remove the cap on the payroll tax, institute income limits on some obligations, cut some military programs, and impose a modest tax increase. The problem is easily solved. What is being done is not a solution.
